version.changelog:
- Updated documentation in README.md and SKILL.md for improved clarity and completeness.
- No functional or command changes; this release focuses on refining usage instructions and examples.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated marketing purpose, but it includes embedded API keys, invokes arbitrary shell commands (chrome/Xvfb/curl), and reaches into a local path for another skill — these mismatches warrant caution before installing or running it.

dimensions.detail: The code and SKILL.md implement TikTok/Douyin analysis, title/script generation, memory storage and optional video-render integration — these features align with the marketing hub description. However the repo ships an embedded TikHub and DeepSeek key in scripts/config.js and the skill attempts to call a local render script under the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2/...), which is not declared in the manifest or SKILL.md as a dependency; that cross-skill/local-path coupling is unexpected for a standalone marketing analysis tool.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs cloning and configuring API tokens (expected) but the runtime code does more than the docs describe: it can launch a real or virtual browser, start Xvfb, run google-chrome, run shell commands (curl/pkill/Xvfb), write memory files, and call an external run_render.py by absolute path in the user's home. Those actions extend scope beyond simple API calls and local analysis and can execute arbitrary binaries on the host.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; this is instruction+code only (no downloaded archives). That limits supply-chain risk from the manifest itself. However the code uses exec/execSync to run external commands — see instruction_scope and subprocess concerns.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Manifest declares no required env vars, but scripts/config.js contains hard-coded tokens (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY). Shipping embedded credentials is a sensitive mismatch: credentials are present in-repo (exfiltration/leak risk) even though no env vars are required. The code uses these secrets to call external APIs via a shell curl and also writes/reads configuration files under scripts/, which increases the risk profile.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest correctly sets always: false. The skill does persist data to scripts/memory/ and writes scripts/config.js (manifest lists those paths under doNotCommitToVcs), which is expected. The concern is that the manifest's subprocess policy only lists node as allowed, but the code executes many other shell commands (chrome, Xvfb, pkill, curl), and it tries to call a script in another skill's workspace — this combination gives the skill potential to run unexpected host-level commands or other skills' code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:
- Do not run this skill on sensitive systems without review: the code executes shell commands (chrome, Xvfb, curl, pkill) and may start processes on your host.
- The repository includes hard-coded API keys in scripts/config.js. Treat those as compromised: remove them and replace with your own tokens or set them via secure environment/configuration before running; rotate any keys if you used them.
- The skill attempts to call a local render script at ~/.openclaw-agent2/... which could execute code from other skills. If you don't want cross-skill execution, remove or sandbox cmd_vid_integration.py or ensure that path does not exist on your machine.
- The manifest restricts subprocesses to node but the code runs many non-node commands — this is an inconsistency. Prefer to run the tool in a controlled environment (container or isolated VM) and inspect/modify the code to remove unwanted shell invocations.
- If you decide to proceed: (1) audit and remove embedded credentials, (2) review and sanitize any exec/execSync calls, (3) run in a disposable environment, and (4) only provide your own API keys after understanding where and how they are used.
llm.findings:
[hard-coded-credential-in-repo] unexpected: scripts/config.js contains TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY values. A marketing analysis skill normally asks the user to provide API tokens (via config or env), but shipping active-looking keys in the repo is unexpected and increases risk of leaked/compromised credentials.
[subprocess-shell-usage] unexpected: marketing_hub.js uses exec/execSync to run curl, start/kill Xvfb, and run google-chrome. Manifest subprocess.allowedPatterns only lists 'node', so the code's use of other shell commands is inconsistent with declared permissions and increases host execution risk.
[local-cross-skill-invoke] unexpected: scripts/cmd_vid_integration.py references an absolute path under ~/.openclaw-agent2/... to run another skill's run_render.py. Calling another skill's code by absolute path is unexpected and could result in executing arbitrary local scripts if present.
